svg.title: Chronos Tokenization vs the TimesFM Patch Decoder
svg.desc: Turning values into discrete tokens and solving it with a language-model architecture, versus embedding continuous patches directly and emitting many steps from a decoder.
svg.text: Chronos Tokenization vs the TimesFM Patch Decoder
Convert values into tokens, or feed continuous patches as they are
Cost scales with the number of samples;
Bolt improved this to a single pass
Many steps at once in a
A quantile head outputs them directly
Bin indices — tokens a language model reads
The number of bins K sets the resolution
Continuous patches embedded as they are
No loss of resolution in the values
Generated by feeding back one step at a time
The last output is the next input
Draw the path repeatedly to build a distribution
Compute grows with the number of samples
Errors can accumulate over long horizons
Many steps in a single forward pass
The quantile head emits the intervals along with it
Compute is largely insensitive to horizon length
Discrete tokens let you reuse language-model machinery; continuous patches preserve resolution.
Recursive or single-pass decoding decides speed and long-horizon stability.
Both train on a large corpus, then
forecast new series by inference alone
